Use the finite-dimensional model of normalized trace. For an algebraic characteristic-zero extension \(L/F\), each element lies in a finite separable subextension, where the normalized trace is
\[
\operatorname{NTr}_{L/F}(x)=\frac{\operatorname{Tr}_{L_0/F}(x)}{[L_0:F]},
\]
independently of the chosen finite subextension \(L_0\).

Organize the two claims as follows:

1. For \(a\in F\), compute in any finite subextension containing \(a\). Ordinary trace sends the scalar \(a\) to \([L_0:F]a\), so normalization gives \(a\).

2. For the tower \(F\subseteq E\subseteq K\), prove equality of the two linear maps by evaluating at \(x\in K\). Reduce the calculation to suitable finite subextensions generated by \(x\) and the finitely many coefficients involved in its trace over \(E\). Then apply transitivity of ordinary field trace and multiplicativity of finite degrees:
\[
\operatorname{Tr}_{K_0/F}
 =\operatorname{Tr}_{E_0/F}\circ\operatorname{Tr}_{K_0/E_0},
\qquad
[K_0:F]=[K_0:E_0][E_0:F].
\]
Dividing by the degrees yields transitivity of normalized trace. Finally identify the inner map as \(F\)-linear via restriction of scalars, matching the stated composition.

Characteristic zero is essential here because it gives separability and makes the positive integer degrees invertible in the base fields; integrality supplies the required finite algebraic subextensions elementwise.
